corrections.form_value: Thirty-six students solved a real-world problem-solving task collaboratively under one of three conditions: immediate AI access, delayed AI access, or no AI access. The author calls the design quasi-experimental. The abstract reports a homogenisation score of the solutions and a level of creativity by condition, without numbers.
corrections.source_says: The methods report random assignment of 36 graduate students to immediate AI access, AI access after 15 minutes of unassisted work, or no AI access. Students worked in 13 collaborative groups (4 immediate, 4 delayed, 5 no AI) on a sustainable water plan for a touristic city in the French Rivera. The reported quantitative outcome is group-level homogenisation of thematic ideas. Preserve the discrepancy between the abstract's quasi-experimental label and the explicit random-assignment statement in Methods.

corrections.source_says: The full text operationalizes homogenisation using content-analysis category counts: identify unique thematic ideas across all groups, count how many groups share each idea, and sum the shared-idea counts for each group's score. Set measure to category_count, unit to team, and n_units to 13; update measure_detail and diversity_detail accordingly. The comparison pool spans all groups, not only groups within the same AI condition. Report the printed group-level descriptives: Immediate AI M = 33.250, SD = 7.932 (4 groups); Delayed AI M = 26.250, SD = 4.272 (4 groups); No AI M = 17.800, SD = 8.379 (5 groups). The numbers of groups are not per-arm people counts. Replace the 'none' statistics entry and 'No numbers in the abstract' limitation with arm_means_sds_ns, explicitly labelling n as groups. These descriptives support Immediate AI versus No AI and Delayed AI versus No AI (ai_vs_bau, treatment_lower on diversity), and Delayed AI versus Immediate AI (ai_design, treatment_higher on diversity). The text describes significant differences but supplies no numerical test statistic, p value, confidence interval, standard error, or standardized effect; Fig. 4 is a boxplot without inferential annotations.

confirmed: Read the complete author-deposited PDF in memory: 5 pages, including references through p. 5; no appendix is included. Author on p. 1 is Margarida Romero. Crossref independently gives proceedings pages 321-325 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109%2FICAITE68636.2025.11442590).
The existing participants.n_randomized = 36 is confirmed by the Methods phrase '36 graduate students were randomly assigned'; this counts people, not outputs or ratings (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology).

The paper does not explicitly report exclusions, analyzed-person totals, or per-arm people counts; keep participants.n_analyzed and the arm people counts null. With only 36 people in the study, fewer than 50 people could be analyzed (PDF pp. 3-4, Methods and Results).

There are 13 collaborative groups: 4 immediate-access, 4 delayed-access, and 5 no-access. Results assess each group's final product; these are group/output analysis units, not participant counts (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology, Fig. 2, and IV. Results).

Delayed access begins after 15 minutes of unassisted ideation; Immediate AI is available from the start, and No AI has no GenAI access throughout. The total activity duration is not reported (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2).

Participants are graduate students developing a sustainable water plan for a touristic city in the French Rivera. That task location does not establish the participants' country, and the paper does not name the GenAI model (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology; full PDF pp. 1-5).

Homogenisation is scored on group-produced solutions, so criterion 3 is met. The across_people diversity construct and reversing the direction of homogenisation to represent diversity are appropriate (PDF p. 3, IV. Results; codebook sections 6-7).

Printed descriptives are Immediate AI M = 33.250, SD = 7.932 (PDF p. 3, IV. Results); Delayed AI M = 26.250, SD = 4.272 and No AI M = 17.800, SD = 8.379 (PDF p. 4, IV. Results). Figure 4 contains boxplots, not an additional numerical significance test.

Both original reported strings accurately reproduce the abstract's qualitative comparisons, including 'significantly more similar solutions' and 'the highest level of creativity'; the abstract contains no outcome estimates. The complete PDF adds descriptive statistics but no numerical inferential tests (PDF p. 1, Abstract; pp. 3-4, Results; independently retrieved OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar abstracts).

This is one original people study, not an AI-versus-human output comparison or a synthesis. Theoretical-framework citations to meta-analyses are background, so leaving synthesis counts and pooled estimates empty is appropriate (PDF pp. 2-4, sections II-IV).

Core exclusion on sample size remains appropriate: the assigned cohort of 36 is below the 50-person threshold. The corrected randomization finding changes screening routing and context classification, not that size-based exclusion (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology; codebook section 3).
summary: Methods report random assignment of 36 graduate students, requiring two-screener review while remaining below the 50-person threshold. The full text provides group-level homogenisation statistics for 13 teams, without a separate creativity score or numerical inferential tests.
